title: Instance administration and Facet approval are deliberately held by different governance proxies
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.2.1 defines the Default Admin Role (`DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`) as the administrative role of an Instance's access-control contract, authorized to grant and revoke all other roles, held by Sky Governance through the Prime Agent's SubProxy. It then flags the distinction explicitly: "This per-Instance role is distinct from the Beacon's own `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which is held by the Pause Proxy."

Both paths terminate in Sky Governance, so this is not a separation of *owners* — it is a separation of *scopes of blast radius*. Actions taken through a Prime Agent's SubProxy affect only that Agent's Instance; actions taken through the Pause Proxy affect the shared Facet registry every Instance depends on.

A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.2.7 repeats the pattern one level down: the Administered Agent Admin controls the AdministeredAgent's own Admins, Grantors, Actors and Revokers, and is "distinct from the Default Admin Role... which administers the Diamond PAU access-control contract; both are held by Sky Governance through the Prime Agent's SubProxy."

The design lesson is that same-principal roles are still worth splitting. Distinct roles make each governance action's reach legible on-chain and let per-Agent operations proceed without touching a lever whose misuse would be ecosystem-wide.
description: A per-Instance DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE sits with the Prime Agent's SubProxy while the Beacon's own admin sits with the Pause Proxy, splitting what an Agent may configure from what it may use.
